optB.titleEn: Describe the construction, working principle, and energy production in a nuclear reactor with a neat schematic diagram.
optB.titleTa: அணுக்கரு உலையின் அமைப்பு, செயல்படும் விதம் மற்றும் ஆற்றல் உற்பத்தியை தகுந்த படத்துடன் விவரிக்க.

scheme.step: Schematic diagram of reactor showing core, fuel rods, control rods, moderator, and coolant
Function of fuel rods ($^{235}\text{U}$), moderator (heavy water/graphite slows fast neutrons)
Function of control rods (Cadmium/Boron absorbs neutrons to maintain $k=1$)
Coolant and radiation shielding mechanism

optB.solution: A nuclear reactor maintains a controlled, self-sustaining nuclear chain fission reaction ($k = 1$). Essential parts: 1. Nuclear Fuel: Fissionable $^{235}\text{U}$ or $^{239}\text{Pu}$ rods. 2. Moderator: Heavy water ($D_2O$) or graphite to thermalize fast neutrons from $2 \text{ MeV}$ to $0.025 \text{ eV}$. 3. Control Rods: Boron or Cadmium rods with high neutron absorption cross-section to regulate reaction rate. 4. Coolant: Water or liquid sodium circulating through core to extract fission thermal energy to produce steam for turbines. 5. Shielding: Thick concrete wall preventing escape of lethal gamma rays and neutrons.

optA.titleEn: Describe the working of an NPN transistor in common emitter (CE) configuration as an amplifier with neat circuit diagram and derive voltage gain.
optA.titleTa: ஒரு NPN டிரான்சிஸ்டர் பொது உமிழ்ப்பான் (CE) சுற்றில் பெருக்கியாகச் செயல்படுவதை மின்சுற்றுப் படத்துடன் விளக்கி மின்னழுத்தப் பெருக்கத்திற்கான கோவையைப் பெறுக.

scheme.step: Circuit diagram showing biased CE NPN transistor with input AC source and output load $R_C$
Explanation of input loop and output loop with $180^\circ$ phase reversal
Current gain $\beta = \frac{\Delta I_C}{\Delta I_B}$ and input resistance $r_i = \frac{\Delta V_{BE}}{\Delta I_B}$
Voltage gain derivation: $A_v = \frac{v_o}{v_i} = -\frac{\Delta I_C R_C}{\Delta I_B r_i} = -\beta \frac{R_C}{r_i}$

optA.solution: Emitter-base junction is forward-biased and collector-base junction is reverse-biased. Input AC signal $v_i$ is applied across base-emitter. During positive half-cycle of input, forward bias increases, increasing base current $I_B$ and collector current $I_C$. Output voltage $V_{CE} = V_{CC} - I_C R_C$ decreases, making the output signal negative (yielding a $180^\circ$ phase shift). Voltage gain: $A_v = \frac{\Delta V_o}{\Delta V_i} = -\frac{\Delta I_C R_C}{\Delta I_B r_i} = -\beta \frac{R_C}{r_i}$.

optB.titleEn: Explain the working of Radar systems and mention any four practical applications of Radar in modern technology.
optB.titleTa: ரேடார் (RADAR) அமைப்பின் செயல்பாட்டை விளக்கி, நவீன தொழில்நுட்பத்தில் ரேடாரின் ஏதேனும் நான்கு பயன்பாடுகளைக் குறிப்பிடுக.

scheme.step: Radar acronym expansion (RAdio Detection And Ranging) & working principle
Echo principle formula for distance: $d = \frac{c \Delta t}{2}$
Four applications: Air traffic control, military defense, weather forecasting, and satellite navigation

optB.solution: RADAR stands for RAdio Detection And Ranging. It transmits high-frequency microwave pulses towards targets. The transmitted pulses strike an obstacle (e.g., aircraft, ship) and reflect back as an echo to the radar receiver. By measuring round-trip travel time $\Delta t$, target distance is calculated: $d = \frac{c \Delta t}{2}$. Applications: 1. Air traffic control (ATC) to guide aircraft landing and avoid mid-air collisions. 2. Military defense for tracking enemy missiles and fighter aircraft. 3. Meteorological weather forecasting to track hurricanes and cyclones. 4. Planetary radar mapping in astronomy.

2026.titleEn: HIGHER SECONDARY SECOND YEAR PUBLIC EXAMINATION - MARCH 2026
2026.titleTa: மேல்நிலை இரண்டாம் ஆண்டு பொதுத் தேர்வு - மார்ச் 2026

part1.en: Two identical conducting spheres having charges $+q$ and $-q$ are separated by a distance $r$. The electrostatic force between them is $F$. If each sphere is given an additional charge of $+2q$, then the new electrostatic force between them will be:
part1.ta: $+q$ மற்றும் $-q$ மின்னூட்டங்களைக் கொண்ட ஒரே மாதிரியான இரு கடத்தும் கோளங்கள் $r$ இடைவெளியில் வைக்கப்பட்டுள்ளன. அவற்றிடையே செயல்படும் நிலைமின் விசை $F$. இப்போது ஒவ்வொரு கோளத்திற்கும் கூடுதலாக $+2q$ மின்னூட்டம் அளிக்கப்பட்டால், அவற்றிடையே செயல்படும் புதிய விசை:
part1.solution: Initial force: $F = -k \frac{q^2}{r^2}$ (attractive). New charges: $q_1' = +q + 2q = +3q$, $q_2' = -q + 2q = +q$. New force: $F' = k \frac{(+3q)(+q)}{r^2} = 3 k \frac{q^2}{r^2} = 3F$ (Repulsive force between like positive charges).

part1.en: A wire of resistance $R$ is stretched uniformly so that its length becomes $n$ times its original length. The new resistance of the wire is:
part1.ta: $R$ மின்தடை கொண்ட ஒரு கம்பி சீராக நீட்டப்பட்டு அதன் நீளம் தொடக்க நீளத்தைப் போல $n$ மடங்காக மாறினால், அதன் புதிய மின்தடை:
part1.solution: Volume remains constant: $V = A_1 L_1 = A_2 L_2$. Since $L_2 = n L_1$, $A_2 = A_1 / n$. Resistance $R' = \rho \frac{L_2}{A_2} = \rho \frac{n L_1}{A_1 / n} = n^2 \rho \frac{L_1}{A_1} = n^2 R$.

part1.en: A charged particle of charge $q$ and mass $m$ enters perpendicularly into a uniform magnetic field $B$ with velocity $v$. The time period of revolution in the circular path is independent of:
part1.ta: $q$ மின்னூட்டமும் $m$ நிறையும் கொண்ட ஒரு மின்துகள் $B$ என்ற சீரான காந்தப்புலத்திற்கு செங்குத்தாக $v$ திசைவேகத்துடன் நுழைகிறது. அது வட்டப்பாதையில் இயங்கும் அலைவுக்காலம் எதனைச் சார்ந்திருக்காது?
part1.solution: Centripetal force equals magnetic Lorentz force: $\frac{m v^2}{r} = q v B \implies r = \frac{m v}{q B}$. Time period $T = \frac{2\pi r}{v} = \frac{2\pi m}{q B}$, which is completely independent of both speed $v$ and radius $r$.

part1.en: In a series LCR alternating current circuit at resonance, the phase angle $\phi$ between voltage and current is:
part1.ta: ஒரு தொடர் LCR மாறுதிசை மின்னோட்டச் சுற்றில் ஒத்திசைவின் போது, மின்னழுத்தம் மற்றும் மின்னோட்டத்திற்கு இடையேயான கட்ட வேறுபாடு $\phi$:
part1.solution: At resonance, inductive reactance equals capacitive reactance ($X_L = X_C$). Hence, impedance $Z = R$. Phase angle $\tan \phi = \frac{X_L - X_C}{R} = 0 \implies \phi = 0$. Current and voltage are in the same phase.

part1.en: Which of the following electromagnetic radiations has the shortest wavelength?
part1.ta: பின்வருவனவற்றுள் மிகக் குறைந்த அலைநீளம் கொண்ட மின்காந்த கதிர்வீச்சு எது?
part1.solution: Gamma rays have the highest frequency ($> 10^{19} \text{ Hz}$) and shortest wavelength ($< 10^{-12} \text{ m}$) in the electromagnetic spectrum.

part1.en: A ray of light traveling in a denser medium of refractive index $n = \sqrt{2}$ strikes the surface at an interface with air. The critical angle for total internal reflection is:
part1.ta: $n = \sqrt{2}$ ஒளிவிலகல் எண் கொண்ட அடர்மிகு ஊடகத்திலிருந்து செல்லும் ஒளிக்கதிர் காற்றுடன் உள்ள இடைமுகத்தைத் தாக்குகிறது. முழு அக எதிரொளிப்பிற்கான மாறுநிலைக்கோணம்:
part1.solution: The relation between critical angle and refractive index: $\sin i_c = \frac{1}{n} = \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} \implies i_c = 45^\circ$.

part1.en: In Young's double-slit experiment, if the separation between the slits is halved and the distance between slits and screen is doubled, the fringe width becomes:
part1.ta: யங் இரட்டைப் பிளவு ஆய்வில், பிளவுகளுக்கு இடையேயான தொலைவு பாதியாகக் குறைக்கப்பட்டு, பிளவுகளுக்கும் திரைக்குமான தொலைவு இருமடங்காக அதிகரிக்கப்பட்டால், பட்டை அகலம்:
part1.solution: Fringe width formula: $\beta = \frac{\lambda D}{d}$. When $D' = 2D$ and $d' = d/2$: $\beta' = \frac{\lambda (2D)}{d/2} = 4 \frac{\lambda D}{d} = 4\beta$.

part1.en: If the kinetic energy of a free electron is doubled, its de Broglie wavelength changes by the factor:
part1.ta: ஒரு தனித்த எலக்ட்ரானின் இயக்க ஆற்றல் இருமடங்கானால், அதன் டி பிராய் அலைநீளம் மாறும் காரணி:
part1.solution: De Broglie wavelength: $\lambda = \frac{h}{\sqrt{2mK}}$. When $K' = 2K$, $\lambda' = \frac{h}{\sqrt{2m(2K)}} = \frac{\lambda}{\sqrt{2}}$.

part1.en: The ratio of minimum to maximum wavelength in the Lyman series of hydrogen spectrum is:
part1.ta: ஹைட்ரஜன் அணு நிறமாலையின் லைமன் தொடரில் சிறும அலைநீளத்திற்கும் பெரும அலைநீளத்திற்குமான தகவு:
part1.solution: Lyman series: $\frac{1}{\lambda} = R \left( \frac{1}{1^2} - \frac{1}{n^2} \right)$. For $\lambda_{\text{min}}$, $n = \infty \implies \lambda_{\text{min}} = \frac{1}{R}$. For $\lambda_{\text{max}}$, $n = 2 \implies \frac{1}{\lambda_{\text{max}}} = R\left(1 - \frac{1}{4}\right) = \frac{3R}{4} \implies \lambda_{\text{max}} = \frac{4}{3R}$. Ratio $\frac{\lambda_{\text{min}}}{\lambda_{\text{max}}} = \frac{3}{4}$.

part1.en: The nuclear density of all stable nuclei is approximately:
part1.ta: அனைத்து நிலையான அணுக்கருக்களின் அணுக்கரு அடர்த்தி தோராயமாக:
part1.solution: Nuclear density $\rho = \frac{\text{Mass}}{\text{Volume}} = \frac{A \cdot m_N}{\frac{4}{3}\pi R_0^3 A} = \frac{3 m_N}{4\pi R_0^3} \approx 2.3 \times 10^{17} \text{ kg m}^{-3}$, completely independent of mass number $A$.

part1.en: In a half-wave rectifier, if the input alternating current frequency is $50 \text{ Hz}$, then the output ripple frequency is:
part1.ta: ஓர் அரை அலை திருத்தியில், உள்ளீட்டு மாறுதிசை மின்னோட்டத்தின் அதிர்வெண் $50 \text{ Hz}$ எனில் வெளியீட்டு அலைவு அதிர்வெண்:
part1.solution: In a half-wave rectifier, one pulse occurs per full AC input cycle, so output frequency equals input frequency: $f_{\text{out}} = f_{\text{in}} = 50 \text{ Hz}$. (In contrast, a full-wave rectifier yields $2f = 100 \text{ Hz}$).

part1.en: The output $Y$ of a logic gate is $1$ only when all its inputs are $0$. The logic gate is:
part1.ta: ஒரு தருக்க வாயிலின் அனைத்து உள்ளீடுகளும் $0$ ஆக இருக்கும்போது மட்டுமே வெளியீடு $Y = 1$ ஆகிறது எனில், அந்த வாயில்:
part1.solution: Boolean expression for NOR gate is $Y = \overline{A + B}$. When $A=0, B=0$, $Y = \overline{0+0} = 1$. For any other input combination containing $1$, the output is $0$.

part1.en: In an amplitude modulated wave, the maximum and minimum amplitudes are $12 \text{ V}$ and $4 \text{ V}$ respectively. The modulation factor (index) $m$ is:
part1.ta: ஒரு வீச்சு மாடுலேற்றம் செய்யப்பட்ட அலையில் பெரும மற்றும் சிறும வீச்சுகள் முறையே $12 \text{ V}$ மற்றும் $4 \text{ V}$ ஆகும். மாடுலேற்றக் காரணி (குறியீடு) $m$ என்பது:
part1.solution: Modulation index $m = \frac{E_{\text{max}} - E_{\text{min}}}{E_{\text{max}} + E_{\text{min}}} = \frac{12 - 4}{12 + 4} = \frac{8}{16} = 0.5$.

part1.en: Kirchhoff's current rule (junction rule) and voltage rule (loop rule) respectively demonstrate the conservation of:
part1.ta: கிர்க்காஃபின் மின்னோட்ட விதி (சந்தி விதி) மற்றும் மின்னழுத்த விதி (சுற்று விதி) ஆகியவை முறையே எதன் மாறா விதிகளை நிரூபிக்கின்றன?
part1.solution: Kirchhoff's first rule (junction rule) $\sum I = 0$ is based on conservation of electric charge. The second rule (loop rule) $\sum IR = \sum \mathcal{E}$ is based on conservation of energy.

part1.en: The magnetic needle suspended freely at the magnetic equator of the Earth comes to rest horizontally. The angle of dip (inclination) at the equator is:
part1.ta: புவியின் காந்த நிலநடுக்கோட்டில் தடையின்றி தொங்கவிடப்பட்ட காந்த ஊசி கிடைமட்டமாக நிற்கிறது. நிலநடுக்கோட்டில் சரிவுக் கோணம் (dip angle):
part1.solution: At the magnetic equator, the magnetic field is purely horizontal ($B_V = 0$). Hence, angle of dip $\theta = \tan^{-1}\left(\frac{B_V}{B_H}\right) = 0^\circ$. At the magnetic poles, dip is $90^\circ$.

part2.en: Define electric flux. Write its SI unit.
part2.ta: மின்பாயம் - வரையறு. அதன் SI அலகை எழுதுக.

scheme.step: Definition: The number of electric field lines crossing a given area held normal to it
Formula: $\Phi_E = \int \vec{E} \cdot d\vec{A}$ and SI Unit: $\text{N m}^2 \text{ C}^{-1}$ (or $\text{V m}$)

part2.solution: Electric flux is defined as the total number of electric field lines passing normally through a given area. SI unit: $\text{N m}^2 \text{ C}^{-1}$ or $\text{V m}$. In Tamil: ஒரு குறிப்பிட்ட பரப்பு வழியே அதற்கு செங்குத்தாகக் கடந்து செல்லும் மின்புலக் கோடுகளின் எண்ணிக்கை மின்பாயம் எனப்படும்.

part2.en: State Fleming's Left Hand Rule.
part2.ta: பிளெமிங்கின் இடக்கை விதியைக் கூறுக.

scheme.step: Stretching forefinger, middle finger, and thumb mutually perpendicular
Forefinger: Magnetic field, Middle finger: Current, Thumb: Force/motion of conductor

part2.solution: Stretch the forefinger, middle finger, and thumb of the left hand mutually perpendicular to one another. If the forefinger points in the direction of magnetic field and middle finger in the direction of electric current, then the thumb indicates the direction of magnetic force acting on the conductor.

part2.en: What is meant by wattless current?
part2.ta: திறனற்ற மின்னோட்டம் என்றால் என்ன?

scheme.step: Statement that current does not consume electrical power ($P = V_{rms} I_{rms} \cos(\pi/2) = 0$)
Condition: In a purely inductive or capacitive circuit where phase angle $\phi = \pi/2$

part2.solution: The current in an AC circuit is said to be wattless current if the average power consumed by the circuit over a complete cycle is zero. This occurs in a purely inductive or capacitive circuit where the phase difference between voltage and current is $\pi/2$ ($\cos 90^\circ = 0$).

part2.en: Write any two applications of microwaves.
part2.ta: நுண்ணலைகளின் (Microwaves) ஏதேனும் இரு பயன்களை எழுதுக.

scheme.step: Point 1: Radar systems for aircraft navigation and speed detection
Point 2: Microwave ovens for domestic and industrial heating / satellite communication

part2.solution: 1. Microwaves are used in radar systems for aircraft navigation, defense surveillance, and detecting vehicle speeds. 2. Used in microwave ovens for rapid dielectric heating of food. 3. Used in long-distance satellite and wireless telecommunication links.

part2.en: State Brewster's Law.
part2.ta: புரூஸ்டர் விதியைக் கூறுக.

scheme.step: Statement: Tangent of the polarizing angle is equal to the refractive index of the medium
Formula: $\tan i_p = n$

part2.solution: Brewster's law states that the tangent of the polarising angle ($i_p$) for a transparent refracting medium is numerically equal to the refractive index ($n$) of the medium: $\tan i_p = n$.

part2.en: Define threshold frequency for photoelectric emission.
part2.ta: ஒளிமின் உமிழ்விற்கான பயன்தொடக்க அதிர்வெண் - வரையறு.

scheme.step: Definition: Minimum frequency of incident light required to liberate photoelectrons
Mention of zero kinetic energy at threshold frequency / symbol $\nu_0$

part2.solution: Threshold frequency ($\nu_0$) is defined as the minimum frequency of incident radiation below which no photoelectrons are emitted from the metal surface, regardless of the intensity of incident radiation.

part2.en: Define mass defect ($\Delta m$).
part2.ta: நிறைக் குறைபாடு ($\Delta m$) - வரையறு.

scheme.step: Difference between the sum of masses of individual nucleons and rest mass of nucleus
Formula: $\Delta m = [Z m_p + (A - Z)m_n] - M$

part2.solution: Mass defect is the difference between the total mass of the individual constituent nucleons (protons and neutrons) forming the nucleus and the actual measured rest mass of the nucleus: $\Delta m = [Z m_p + (A - Z)m_n] - M_{\text{nucleus}}$.

part2.en: What is rectification? Name the two types of rectifiers.
part2.ta: திருத்துதல் என்றால் என்ன? இரு வகையான திருத்திகளின் பெயர்களைக் குறிப்பிடுக.

scheme.step: Definition: Process of converting AC voltage into pulsating DC voltage
Types: Half-wave rectifier and Full-wave rectifier

part2.solution: The process of converting an alternating current (AC) into direct current (DC) using a p-n junction diode is called rectification. The two types are: (i) Half-wave rectifier and (ii) Full-wave rectifier (centre-tapped or bridge type).

part2.en: [Compulsory] Calculate the de Broglie wavelength of an electron accelerated through an electric potential difference of $100 \text{ V}$.
part2.ta: [கட்டாய வினா] $100 \text{ V}$ மின்னழுத்த வேறுபாட்டினால் முடுக்கப்படும் எலக்ட்ரானின் டி பிராய் அலைநீளத்தைக் கணக்கிடுக.

scheme.step: Formula: $\lambda = \frac{12.27}{\sqrt{V}} \text{ Å}$ or $\lambda = \frac{h}{\sqrt{2 m e V}}$
Substitution & Final Answer: $\lambda = \frac{12.27}{\sqrt{100}} = 1.227 \text{ Å} = 0.1227 \text{ nm}$

part2.solution: Formula: $\lambda = \frac{h}{\sqrt{2 m e V}} = \frac{12.27}{\sqrt{V}} \text{ Å}$. Given $V = 100 \text{ V}$. $\lambda = \frac{12.27}{\sqrt{100}} = \frac{12.27}{10} = 1.227 \text{ Å} = 1.227 \times 10^{-10} \text{ m}$ (or $0.1227 \text{ nm}$).

part3.en: Derive the relation between electric field $\vec{E}$ and electrostatic potential $V$.
part3.ta: மின்புலம் $\vec{E}$ மற்றும் மின்னழுத்தம் $V$ ஆகியவற்றுக்கு இடையேயான தொடர்பை பெறுக.

scheme.step: Work done in moving test charge: $dW = -q_0 E \, dx$
Potential difference relation: $dV = \frac{dW}{q_0} = -E \, dx$
Final relation: $E = -\frac{dV}{dx}$ with negative sign physical significance

part3.solution: Work done to move a test charge $q_0$ by $dx$ against electric field: $dW = \vec{F} \cdot d\vec{x} = -q_0 E \, dx$. Potential difference: $dV = \frac{dW}{q_0} = -E \, dx \implies E = -\frac{dV}{dx}$. The electric field is the negative gradient of electric potential.

part3.en: Obtain the macroscopic form of Ohm's law from microscopic relation between current density and drift velocity.
part3.ta: மின்னோட்ட அடர்த்தி மற்றும் இழுப்புத் திசைவேகம் இடையேயான தொடர்பிலிருந்து ஓம் விதியின் நுண்மாதிரி மற்றும் பயன்பாட்டு வடிவத்தைப் பெறுக.

scheme.step: Microscopic relation: $J = n e v_d$
Substituting $v_d = \frac{e\tau}{m}E \implies J = \left(\frac{n e^2 \tau}{m}\right)E = \sigma E$
Macroscopic conversion: $I = J A = \frac{\sigma A}{L}V \implies V = I R$

part3.solution: Current $I = n e A v_d$. Current density $J = I/A = n e v_d$. Since $v_d = \frac{e \tau}{m} E$, $J = \frac{n e^2 \tau}{m} E = \sigma E$. Substituting $E = V/L$ and $J = I/A$ gives $\frac{I}{A} = \sigma \frac{V}{L} \implies V = I \left(\frac{L}{\sigma A}\right) = I R$.

part3.en: State and explain Biot-Savart Law in vector form.
part3.ta: பயோட்-சாவர்ட் விதியைக் கூறி வெக்டர் வடிவில் விளக்குக.

scheme.step: Statement of law ($dB \propto I, dl, \sin\theta, 1/r^2$)
Scalar equation: $dB = \frac{\mu_0}{4\pi} \frac{I dl \sin\theta}{r^2}$
Vector form: $d\vec{B} = \frac{\mu_0}{4\pi} \frac{I (d\vec{l} \times \hat{r})}{r^2}$

part3.solution: Biot-Savart law states that the magnetic field $d\vec{B}$ due to a current element $I d\vec{l}$ at a distance $r$ is: $d\vec{B} = \frac{\mu_0}{4\pi} \frac{I(d\vec{l} \times \hat{r})}{r^2}$. Magnitude: $dB = \frac{\mu_0}{4\pi} \frac{I dl \sin\theta}{r^2}$, directed perpendicular to the plane containing $d\vec{l}$ and $\hat{r}$.

part3.en: Mention the various energy losses occurring in a real transformer and explain how each is minimized.
part3.ta: ஒரு நடைமுறை மின்மாற்றியில் ஏற்படும் பல்வேறு ஆற்றல் இழப்புகளைக் குறிப்பிட்டு, அவை எவ்வாறு குறைக்கப்படுகின்றன என்பதை விளக்குக.

scheme.step: Hysteresis loss (minimized by using soft iron core of low retentivity)
Eddy current loss (minimized using laminated core sheets insulated by varnish)
Copper loss ($I^2R$ minimized with thick copper wires) & Flux leakage

part3.solution: 1. Core/Iron loss: (a) Hysteresis loss minimized by using high permeability soft iron / Mumetal with thin hysteresis loop; (b) Eddy current loss minimized by laminating the core. 2. Copper loss: $I^2R$ heating loss minimized by using thick wire for windings. 3. Flux leakage minimized by winding primary and secondary coils one over another.

part3.en: State the laws of refraction (Snell's Law).
part3.ta: ஒளிவிலகல் விதிகளை (ஸ்நெல் விதி) கூறுக.

scheme.step: First law: Incident ray, refracted ray, and normal lie in the same plane
Second law (Snell's law): $\frac{\sin i}{\sin r} = \frac{n_2}{n_1} = n_{21}$

part3.solution: 1. The incident ray, refracted ray, and normal to the interface at the point of incidence all lie in the same plane. 2. The ratio of the sine of the angle of incidence ($i$) to the sine of the angle of refraction ($r$) is a constant equal to the relative refractive index of the second medium with respect to the first: $\frac{\sin i}{\sin r} = \frac{n_2}{n_1}$.

part3.en: State the fundamental laws of photoelectric emission.
part3.ta: ஒளிமின் உமிழ்வின் அடிப்படை விதிகளைக் கூறுக.

scheme.step: Law 1: Photoelectric current is directly proportional to intensity of incident light
Law 2: Maximum kinetic energy depends linearly on frequency, independent of intensity
Law 3: Threshold frequency condition & instantaneous emission ($< 10^{-9} \text{ s}$)

part3.solution: 1. Rate of photoelectron emission is directly proportional to intensity of incident light for a given frequency. 2. Maximum kinetic energy of photoelectrons is independent of intensity and increases linearly with incident frequency. 3. Photoelectric emission does not occur below threshold frequency $\nu_0$. 4. The emission process is instantaneous ($10^{-9} \text{ s}$).

part3.en: Distinguish between nuclear fission and nuclear fusion reactions.
part3.ta: அணுக்கரு பிளவு மற்றும் அணுக்கரு இணைவு வினைகளை வேறுபடுத்துக.

scheme.step: Fission: Heavy nucleus splits into two lighter nuclei; Fusion: Two light nuclei fuse into heavy nucleus
Temperature: Fission at room temp; Fusion requires extremely high temp ($> 10^7 \text{ K}$)
Examples with reactions ($^{235}\text{U}$ fission vs $p-p$ cycle in stars)

part3.solution: Nuclear Fission: Heavy nucleus (like $^{235}\text{U}$) splits into two moderate nuclei with neutron emission at room temp. Nuclear Fusion: Two light nuclei (like Deuterium) combine under ultra-high temperatures ($10^7\text{ K}$) and high pressures to form a heavier nucleus ($^4\text{He}$), releasing much larger energy per unit mass.

part3.en: Explain the action of a Zener diode as a DC voltage regulator with a neat circuit schematic.
part3.ta: செனார் டையோடு ஒரு மின்னழுத்த சீரமைப்பானாக செயல்படும் விதத்தை தகுந்த மின்சுற்றுப் படத்துடன் விளக்குக.

scheme.step: Circuit diagram showing reverse-biased Zener with series resistance $R_s$ and load $R_L$
Explanation of breakdown region where Zener voltage $V_Z$ remains constant
Equations: $V_{in} = I R_s + V_Z$, $I = I_Z + I_L$ demonstrating constant $V_{out} = V_Z$

part3.solution: The Zener diode is operated in its reverse breakdown region. When input DC voltage $V_{in}$ fluctuates, current through Zener diode $I_Z$ changes significantly, but the voltage drop across the Zener diode remains constant at the Zener breakdown voltage $V_Z$. Hence, the output voltage across the load resistor $R_L$ remains steady: $V_{out} = V_Z$.

part3.en: [Compulsory] An electron revolves in the first Bohr orbit of hydrogen atom of radius $0.53 \text{ Å}$ with a speed of $2.2 \times 10^6 \text{ m s}^{-1}$. Calculate the orbital magnetic dipole moment of the revolving electron. (Given $e = 1.6 \times 10^{-19} \text{ C}$).
part3.ta: [கட்டாய வினா] ஹைட்ரஜன் அணுவின் $0.53 \text{ Å}$ ஆரம் கொண்ட முதல் போர் வட்டப்பாதையில் ஓர் எலக்ட்ரான் $2.2 \times 10^6 \text{ m s}^{-1}$ வேகத்தில் சுற்றுகிறது. சுற்றும் எலக்ட்ரானின் சுற்றுப்பாதை காந்த இருமுனைத் திருப்புத்திறனைக் கணக்கிடுக. ($e = 1.6 \times 10^{-19} \text{ C}$).

scheme.step: Current formula: $I = \frac{e}{T} = \frac{e v}{2\pi r}$
Magnetic moment formula: $\mu_L = I A = \left(\frac{e v}{2\pi r}\right) (\pi r^2) = \frac{1}{2} e v r$

part3.solution: Orbital current: $I = \frac{e}{T} = \frac{e v}{2\pi r}$. Orbital magnetic moment: $\mu_L = I A = I(\pi r^2) = \frac{1}{2} e v r$. Calculation: $\mu_L = 0.5 \times (1.6 \times 10^{-19} \text{ C}) \times (2.2 \times 10^6 \text{ m/s}) \times (0.53 \times 10^{-10} \text{ m}) = 9.328 \times 10^{-24} \text{ A m}^2$ (or $\text{J T}^{-1}$).

optA.titleEn: Derive an expression for the electric field due to an electric dipole at a point on its axial line.
optA.titleTa: மின் இருமுனையின் அச்சுக் கோட்டில் உள்ள ஒரு புள்ளியில் மின்புலத்திற்கான கோவையைத் தருவிக்க.

scheme.step: Neat labeled diagram of dipole with charges $+q, -q$ separated by $2a$ and axial point $P$ at distance $r$
Electric field components: $E_+ = \frac{1}{4\pi\epsilon_0}\frac{q}{(r-a)^2}$ and $E_- = \frac{1}{4\pi\epsilon_0}\frac{q}{(r+a)^2}$
Vector addition & simplification: $E_{tot} = \frac{q}{4\pi\epsilon_0}\left[\frac{4ar}{(r^2-a^2)^2}\right]$
Far-field approximation ($r \gg a$): $\vec{E}_{axial} = \frac{1}{4\pi\epsilon_0}\frac{2\vec{p}}{r^3}$

optA.solution: Consider an electric dipole consisting of $-q$ and $+q$ separated by distance $2a$. Let $P$ be a point on axial line at distance $r$ from midpoint $O$. $E_+ = \frac{1}{4\pi\epsilon_0}\frac{q}{(r-a)^2}$ along $\vec{p}$. $E_- = \frac{1}{4\pi\epsilon_0}\frac{q}{(r+a)^2}$ opposite to $\vec{p}$. Resultant: $E = E_+ - E_- = \frac{q}{4\pi\epsilon_0} \left[ \frac{1}{(r-a)^2} - \frac{1}{(r+a)^2} \right] = \frac{q}{4\pi\epsilon_0} \left[ \frac{4ar}{(r^2-a^2)^2} \right]$. Since dipole moment $p = 2aq$, for $r \gg a$, $\vec{E}_{axial} = \frac{1}{4\pi\epsilon_0} \frac{2\vec{p}}{r^3}$.

optB.titleEn: State Kirchhoff's rules and obtain the balancing condition for Wheatstone's bridge network.
optB.titleTa: கிர்க்காஃபின் விதிகளைக் கூறி, வீட்ஸ்டோன் சமனச் சுற்றின் சமன்செய் நிலையைத் தருவிக்க.

scheme.step: Statement of Kirchhoff's Current Rule and Voltage Rule
Circuit diagram of Wheatstone bridge ($P, Q, R, S$ and galvanometer $G$)
Applying loop rule to loops ABDA and BCDB under balanced null deflection ($I_G = 0$)
Derivation of balance ratio: $\frac{P}{Q} = \frac{R}{S}$

optB.solution: Kirchhoff's Rules: 1. Current rule: $\sum I = 0$ at any node. 2. Voltage rule: $\sum IR = \sum \mathcal{E}$ in a closed loop. For Wheatstone bridge, when galvanometer shows zero deflection ($I_G = 0$), junction rules give $I_1 = I_3$ and $I_2 = I_4$. Loop ABDA: $I_1 P - I_2 R = 0 \implies I_1 P = I_2 R$. Loop BCDB: $I_3 Q - I_4 S = 0 \implies I_1 Q = I_2 S$. Dividing the two equations yields: $\frac{P}{Q} = \frac{R}{S}$.

optA.titleEn: Explain the construction and working of a Cyclotron in detail with neat schematic diagram.
optA.titleTa: சைக்ளோட்ரானின் அமைப்பு மற்றும் செயல்படும் விதத்தை படத்துடன் விரிவாக விளக்குக.

scheme.step: Neat diagram showing dees $D_1, D_2$, magnetic poles, target, and deflector plate
Principle: Resonance condition between particle cyclotron frequency and high-frequency oscillator
Working: Electric field accelerates ion across gap; perpendicular magnetic field bends into semi-circles
Mathematical derivation of frequency $f = \frac{qB}{2\pi m}$ and maximum kinetic energy $K_{max} = \frac{q^2 B^2 R^2}{2m}$

optA.solution: Principle: Magnetic Lorentz force provides centripetal acceleration ($m v^2 / r = q v B \implies r = mv / qB$) while high-frequency electric field between the two hollow D-shaped metallic dees accelerates the positive ion every half-cycle. Frequency $f = \frac{qB}{2\pi m}$ is constant (independent of velocity and radius). Maximum kinetic energy: $K = \frac{1}{2} m v_{max}^2 = \frac{q^2 B^2 R^2}{2m}$.

optB.titleEn: Explain the construction, working principle, and energy efficiency of a transformer.
optB.titleTa: மின்மாற்றியின் அமைப்பு, செயல்படும் தத்துவம் மற்றும் பயனுறு திறனை விளக்குக.

scheme.step: Principle (Mutual Induction) and neat diagram of laminated soft iron core with coils
Working equations: $\frac{V_s}{V_p} = \frac{N_s}{N_p} = k$ (Voltage transformation ratio)
Current relation for ideal transformer ($V_p I_p = V_s I_s \implies \frac{I_p}{I_s} = \frac{V_s}{V_p}$)
Definition and formula for efficiency $\eta = \frac{\text{Output Power}}{\text{Input Power}} \times 100\%$

optB.solution: A transformer works on mutual induction. Let $N_p$ and $N_s$ be primary and secondary turns. Rate of flux change $\frac{d\Phi}{dt}$ is identical per turn. Induced voltages: $V_p = -N_p \frac{d\Phi}{dt}$ and $V_s = -N_s \frac{d\Phi}{dt} \implies \frac{V_s}{V_p} = \frac{N_s}{N_p} = k$. For an ideal transformer with zero energy loss: $P_{in} = P_{out} \implies V_p I_p = V_s I_s \implies \frac{I_p}{I_s} = \frac{V_s}{V_p} = k$. Efficiency: $\eta = \frac{P_{out}}{P_{in}} \times 100\% = \frac{V_s I_s}{V_p I_p} \times 100\%$.

optA.titleEn: Derive the mirror equation for a concave mirror and obtain the magnification formula.
optA.titleTa: குழி ஆடிக்கான ஆடிச் சமன்பாட்டைத் தருவித்து பக்கவாட்டு உருப்பெருக்கத்திற்கான கோவையைப் பெறுக.

scheme.step: Ray diagram showing concave mirror, object $AB$, real image $A'B'$, focus $F$, and pole $P$
Geometry of similar triangles $\triangle ABP \sim \triangle A'B'P$ and $\triangle ABF \sim \triangle MPF$
Application of Cartesian sign convention and algebraic steps
Final mirror equation: $\frac{1}{f} = \frac{1}{v} + \frac{1}{u}$ and magnification $m = -\frac{v}{u}$

optA.solution: From similar triangles $\triangle A'B'P \sim \triangle ABP$: $\frac{A'B'}{AB} = \frac{PB'}{PB}$. Using Cartesian sign convention: $AB = +h$, $A'B' = -h'$, $PB = -u$, $PB' = -v$, $PF = -f$. Thus $\frac{-h'}{h} = \frac{-v}{-u} \implies m = \frac{h'}{h} = -\frac{v}{u}$. Similarly, from focus triangles: $\frac{A'B'}{AB} = \frac{B'F}{PF} = \frac{PB' - PF}{PF} = \frac{-v - (-f)}{-f} = \frac{v - f}{f}$. Equating both expressions gives $\frac{v}{u} = \frac{v - f}{f} = \frac{v}{f} - 1$. Dividing both sides by $v$: $\frac{1}{u} = \frac{1}{f} - \frac{1}{v} \implies \frac{1}{f} = \frac{1}{u} + \frac{1}{v}$.

optB.titleEn: Obtain the equation for bandwidth of interference fringes in Young's double-slit experiment.
optB.titleTa: யங் இரட்டைப் பிளவு ஆய்வில் பெறப்படும் குறுக்கீட்டுப் பட்டை அகலத்திற்கான கோவையைத் தருவிக்க.

scheme.step: Experimental schematic showing slits $S_1, S_2$ separated by $d$, screen at $D$, and point $P$
Path difference derivation: $\delta = S_2 P - S_1 P = \frac{y d}{D}$
Condition for bright fringes: $\frac{y_n d}{D} = n \lambda \implies y_n = \frac{n \lambda D}{d}$
Bandwidth deduction: $\beta = y_{n+1} - y_n = \frac{\lambda D}{d}$

optB.solution: Path difference between light waves from slits $S_1$ and $S_2$ arriving at point $P(y)$ on screen: $\delta = S_2 P - S_1 P \approx \frac{y d}{D}$. For constructive interference (bright fringe): $\delta = n \lambda \implies \frac{y_n d}{D} = n \lambda \implies y_n = \frac{n \lambda D}{d}$. Fringe width $\beta$ is the distance between two successive bright (or dark) fringes: $\beta = y_{n+1} - y_n = \frac{(n+1)\lambda D}{d} - \frac{n\lambda D}{d} = \frac{\lambda D}{d}$.

optA.titleEn: State the postulates of Bohr's hydrogen atom model and derive the expression for radius of the $n^{\text{th}}$ orbit.
optA.titleTa: போர் ஹைட்ரஜன் அணு மாதிரியின் எடுகோள்களைக் கூறி, $n$-வது வட்டப்பாதையின் ஆரத்திற்கான கோவையைப் பெறுக.

scheme.step: Stating Bohr's 3 postulates (circular orbits, angular momentum quantization $L = \frac{n h}{2\pi}$, and frequency condition)
Centripetal force balancing electrostatic attraction: $\frac{m v^2}{r} = \frac{1}{4\pi\epsilon_0}\frac{e^2}{r^2}$
Substituting velocity from quantization condition: $v = \frac{n h}{2\pi m r}$
Final radius expression: $r_n = \frac{\epsilon_0 h^2 n^2}{\pi m e^2} = a_0 n^2$ where $a_0 = 0.53 \text{ Å}$

optA.solution: Postulates: 1. Electron moves in non-radiating stationary circular orbits. 2. Angular momentum quantization: $m v r = \frac{n h}{2\pi} \implies v = \frac{n h}{2\pi m r}$. 3. Radiation occurs during transition: $E_2 - E_1 = h\nu$. Force balance: $\frac{m v^2}{r} = \frac{1}{4\pi\epsilon_0} \frac{e^2}{r^2} \implies m v^2 r = \frac{e^2}{4\pi\epsilon_0}$. Substitute $v$: $m \left(\frac{n h}{2\pi m r}\right)^2 r = \frac{e^2}{4\pi\epsilon_0} \implies \frac{n^2 h^2}{4\pi^2 m r} = \frac{e^2}{4\pi\epsilon_0} \implies r_n = \frac{\epsilon_0 h^2 n^2}{\pi m e^2}$. For $n=1$, $r_1 = a_0 = 0.529 \text{ Å}$.

optB.titleEn: State the law of radioactive decay. Derive the exponential decay law $N = N_0 e^{-\lambda t}$ and deduce expressions for half-life and mean life.
optB.titleTa: கதிரியக்கச் சிதைவு விதியைக் கூறுக. $N = N_0 e^{-\lambda t}$ என்ற அடுக்குக்குறி விதியைத் தருவித்து அரை ஆயுட்காலம் மற்றும் சராசரி ஆயுட்காலத்திற்கான சமன்பாடுகளைப் பெறுக.

scheme.step: Statement of law: $\frac{dN}{dt} \propto -N \implies \frac{dN}{dt} = -\lambda N$
Integration and derivation of $N(t) = N_0 e^{-\lambda t}$
Half-life deduction: At $t = T_{1/2}$, $N = N_0/2 \implies T_{1/2} = \frac{\ln 2}{\lambda} = \frac{0.693}{\lambda}$
Mean life deduction: $\tau = \frac{1}{\lambda} = \frac{T_{1/2}}{0.693} = 1.44 T_{1/2}$

optB.solution: Law: Rate of disintegration at any instant is directly proportional to number of nuclei present: $-\frac{dN}{dt} = \lambda N \implies \frac{dN}{N} = -\lambda dt$. Integrating from $t=0$ ($N=N_0$) to $t$ ($N$): $\ln\left(\frac{N}{N_0}\right) = -\lambda t \implies N(t) = N_0 e^{-\lambda t}$. Half-life: when $N = N_0 / 2$, $\frac{1}{2} = e^{-\lambda T_{1/2}} \implies T_{1/2} = \frac{\ln 2}{\lambda} = \frac{0.693}{\lambda}$. Mean life: $\tau = \frac{1}{\lambda} = \frac{T_{1/2}}{0.693} \approx 1.443 T_{1/2}$.

optA.titleEn: Explain the construction and working of a full-wave center-tapped rectifier with neat circuit schematic and input/output waveforms.
optA.titleTa: மையத்தட்டு மின்மாற்றி கொண்ட முழு அலை திருத்தியின் அமைப்பு மற்றும் செயல்படும் விதத்தை மின்சுற்று மற்றும் அலைவடிவங்களுடன் விளக்குக.

scheme.step: Complete circuit diagram with step-down center-tapped transformer, diodes $D_1, D_2$, and load $R_L$
Working during positive half cycle ($D_1$ forward, $D_2$ reverse biased)
Working during negative half cycle ($D_2$ forward, $D_1$ reverse biased)
Input and Output Waveforms and efficiency expression ($\eta = 81.2\%$)

optA.solution: A full-wave center-tapped rectifier utilizes two diodes $D_1$ and $D_2$. During positive half-cycle of AC input: terminal A is positive and B is negative with respect to center tap. Diode $D_1$ is forward-biased and conducts, while $D_2$ is reverse-biased. Current flows through load $R_L$ from top to bottom. During negative half-cycle: terminal B is positive and A is negative. Diode $D_2$ becomes forward-biased and conducts, while $D_1$ is cut off. Current flows through $R_L$ in the same direction. Efficiency $\eta = \frac{P_{dc}}{P_{ac}} = \frac{0.812 R_L}{r_f + R_L} \approx 81.2\%$.

optB.titleEn: Draw the block diagram of a generalized communication system and explain the functions of each block.
optB.titleTa: ஒரு பொதுவான தகவல் தொடர்பு அமைப்பின் தொகுப்பு வரைபடம் வரைந்து ஒவ்வொரு தொகுதியின் செயல்பாட்டையும் விளக்குக.

scheme.step: Neat block diagram: Information Source $\rightarrow$ Transmitter $\rightarrow$ Channel (Noise) $\rightarrow$ Receiver $\rightarrow$ User
Explanation of Information source, Input transducer, and Transmitter
Explanation of Channel, Noise source, and Receiver (Demodulator/Output transducer)

optB.solution: 1. Information Source: Generates the message signal (voice, text, video). 2. Input Transducer: Converts non-electrical physical information into electrical signal. 3. Transmitter: Modulates and amplifies the message signal for propagation through the medium. 4. Transmission Channel: Physical transmission medium (optical fiber, coaxial cable, or free space) where noise gets added. 5. Receiver: Picks up the attenuated signal, separates noise, and demodulates the signal. 6. Output Transducer: Converts electrical signal back into intelligible physical format for user.
